column1: # ACP 18-type atom classification: (residue name, atom name) -> type label.
# PROVENANCE -- READ THIS BEFORE USING OR CITING THE TABLE
#   Kozakov et al. (Proteins 65:392–406, 2006) adopted the 18 ACP atom types
#   from Zhang et al. (J Mol Biol 267:707–726, 1997). They distinguish the
#   four backbone atom types and describe the principal hydrophobic side-chain
#   categories. Table I supplies the labels used in the reconstruction below.
#   (a) The 18 type labels themselves, which are exemplar atoms and therefore
#       self-documenting: `KNz` is lysine N-zeta, `LCd` is leucine C-delta,
#       `GCa` is glycine C-alpha, and so on. The label set is transcribed --
#       it comes from Table I of the PIPER preprint via
#       `data/potentials/dars_acp18.tsv`, and the ordering here matches that
#       file exactly, which is a hard requirement (see CHECKED below).
#   (b) Standard organic and protein chemistry: element, hybridisation, formal
#       charge state at pH 7, hydrogen-bonding role, aromaticity.
#   (c) Two explicit constraints from Kozakov et al. --
#       backbone N/CA/C/O are separate types, and the bulk of hydrophobic
#       side-chain carbon sits in FCz and LCd.
#   (d) The internal structure of the DARS matrix itself, used as a consistency
#       check rather than as a source. See CHECKED item 5.
#   The classification rules actually applied are stated in full below, so that
#   a reviewer can audit the *rule* rather than re-deriving 167 decisions.
#   R1  Backbone N, CA, C, O are their own types.        [preprint p.20, explicit]
#   R2  Glycine CA -> GCa. Glycine's alpha carbon is a methylene, not a
#       methine, and the type list carries a dedicated label for it.
#   R3  C-beta -> Cb, for every residue that has one. The class is *named*
#       C-beta; taking the name literally is what makes the rule auditable.
#   R4  An sp2 carbon bonded to oxygen -- side-chain amide or carboxyl carbon
#       (ASN CG, GLN CD, ASP CG, GLU CD) -> C, the same class as the backbone
#       carbonyl carbon it is chemically identical to.
#   R5  An amide carbonyl oxygen (ASN OD1, GLN OE1) -> O, likewise.
#   R6  A carboxylate oxygen (ASP OD1/OD2, GLU OE1/OE2, and OXT) -> DOd.
#   R7  An aromatic ring carbon -> FCz, except TYR CZ, which bears the hydroxyl
#       and has its own label -> YCz.
#   R8  An aliphatic carbon at gamma or beyond that is terminal or branched
#       (a methyl, or the branch carbon of a beta-branched side chain) -> LCd.
#       A mid-chain methylene at gamma or delta not adjacent to a formal charge
#       -> Cb.  **This is the least certain rule in the file; see LIMITATIONS.**
#   R9  A carbon belonging to the formally charged terminus of a LYS or ARG
#       side chain (LYS CD, CE; ARG CD, CZ) -> KCd. The exemplar that names the
#       class is lysine C-delta, so LYS CD is fixed by the label; CE, and ARG's
#       CD and CZ, follow it by the same chemistry.
#   R10 A formally charged sp3 amine nitrogen (LYS NZ) -> KNz.
#   R11 The guanidinium nitrogens have two labels of their own: ARG NE -> RNe,
#   R12 A side-chain amide nitrogen (ASN ND2, GLN NE2) -> NNd.
#   R13 An aromatic / imidazole nitrogen (HIS ND1, NE2; TRP NE1) -> HNe.
#   R14 A hydroxyl oxygen (SER OG, THR OG1, TYR OH) -> SOg.
#   R15 Sulfur, and its selenium isostere (CYS SG, MET SD, MSE SE) -> CSg.
#   1. **The table has exactly 167 (residue, atom) rows over the 20 standard
#      residues.** This is not a coincidence and it is the strongest available
#      completeness check: the PIPER preprint states that "the existing
#      pairwise interaction potentials can have up to 167 atom types"
#      (PDF p.12), which is precisely the number of distinct heavy atoms in
#      the 20 standard amino acids. A miscount in either direction would show
#   2. Every one of the 18 labels is used at least once.
#   3. The labels, and their order, agree exactly with the header of
#      two files must never drift, because the type index is what indexes the
#   4. Each residue's atom set was checked against standard PDB v3 atom
#      nomenclature, and every atom of every residue is present exactly once.
#   5. **Direction check against the DARS matrix.** LCd-LCd is -1.98, the most
#      attractive non-artefact entry in the matrix, and Cb-Cb is only -0.25.
#      That is what a split into "terminal hydrophobic methyl" (buried, strong)
#      versus "mid-chain methylene" (mixed exposure, weak) predicts, and it is
#      the reason R8 puts terminal carbons in LCd rather than lumping all
#      post-beta aliphatics together. Likewise KCd-KCd is +1.37 and KCd-KNz is
#      +1.34, the most repulsive entries after KNz-KNz, which is what a
#      "carbon attached to a formal charge" class should look like. These are
#      consistency checks on a reconstruction, **not** independent evidence:
#      a different assignment that produced the same signs would be equally
# LIMITATIONS -- the specific places this is most likely to be wrong
#   L1. **The mid-chain methylenes (rule R8) are the largest open ambiguity.**
#       Eight atom types are affected -- PRO CG, PRO CD, LEU CG, ILE CG1,
#       MET CG, GLN CG, GLU CG, LYS CG, ARG CG -- and each could plausibly sit
#       in Cb (as here) or in LCd. They are roughly 6% of the heavy atoms of a
#       typical protein. Nothing in the preprint discriminates.
#   L2. The preprint's remark that "most hydrophobic side chain atoms are in
#       the FCz and LCd categories" is satisfied here by type count
#       (FCz 23 + LCd 8 = 31 against Cb's 28) but **not** by atom count in a
#       typical protein, where Cb is the larger class. If that sentence is read
#       as a constraint rather than as loose description, it argues for moving
#       some of L1's atoms into LCd. It was not treated as a constraint,
#       because it is a descriptive aside in a paper that has already told the
#       reader to look elsewhere for the definition.
#   L3. HIS ring carbons are all FCz, and HIS is treated as neutral. An 18-type
#       scheme has no label for an imidazole carbon flanked by two nitrogens
#       (CE1), so it goes with the aromatics.
#   L4. Positional context is deliberately absent. This is a pure
#       (residue, atom) table, which is what makes it swappable against
#       Zhang et al. without touching code. Two consequences: the N-terminal
#       nitrogen is typed `N` although it is a charged amine, and the
#       C-terminal backbone oxygen is typed `O` although it is half of a
#       carboxylate whose other half (OXT) is typed `DOd`. Both are one atom
#       second case if you want it; it is off by default, because layering an
#       uncited refinement on an uncited reconstruction compounds rather than
#   L5. MSE (selenomethionine) is included because it is the most common
#       modified residue in the PDB and dropping it would silently delete a
#       buried hydrophobic side chain. It is **not** part of the 167 and is not
#       in Zhang et al.'s scheme at all; SE is assigned to CSg as sulfur's
#       isostere. Any other modified residue is dropped by the reader and
#   Comments start with `#`; blank lines ignored.
#   A residue name of `*` matches any residue, and is consulted only when no
#   exact (residue, atom) row exists. It exists for OXT, which every residue
#   can carry and no residue carries in its own right.
#   Names are PDB v3 nomenclature, uppercase, whitespace already stripped.
